_about: Jev-Style guard settings. Keys starting with '_' are notes and are ignored. Environment overrides: JEV_STYLE_GUARD_CONFIG (another file), JEV_STYLE_GUARD_URL, JEV_STYLE_GUARD_LOG, JEV_STYLE_GUARD_DRY_RUN=1, JEV_STYLE_GUARD_DISABLE=1.
_server_url: Only loopback hosts are accepted unless allow_remote_server is true, because the full command is sent to the server.
_dry_run: true = compute and log the verdict, print nothing (Claude Code behaves as if the hook were absent).
_emit_allow: false = an 'allow' verdict prints nothing, so Claude Code's normal permission prompts still apply. true = the guard auto-approves calls it judges safe.
_on_error: Verdict when the server is down, times out, or rejects the request: 'ask' or 'deny' (never 'allow').
_max_field_chars: 0 (default) = never shorten: the whole call is sent, and a call too big for the model's 25,600-token context comes back as input_budget_exceeded, which becomes 'ask'. A positive value shortens longer strings with a visible marker, and any shortened call is raised to at least 'ask' because the model did not see all of it.
_drop_fields: Top-level argument names hidden from the model, per tool ('*' = every tool). Bash's description is the agent's own account of the command and must not talk the guard into anything. Nested keys are never dropped.

thresholds._about: noul answers are P(true) in [0,1]; 'risk' is the expected level index in [0,4] (none, low, moderate, high, severe). A value at or above 'deny' denies, else at or above 'ask' asks. null disables a bound. The strictest verdict across questions wins.

_hard_rules: Regexes checked in code before the model (on the Bash command, or on the JSON arguments for other tools; 'tools' omitted = every tool). They can only make a verdict stricter, never looser.
